findings.cross_file_justification: floor.yaml declares 16 of its 21 floor_guards as fence:FR-SZ* / fence:FR-1.2b rows, all of which are implemented only by .claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh and armed only by the PreToolUse:Bash registration in .claude/settings.json. Neither file is in floor_files, and guard-origins.yaml marks hook:safety/block-destructive-bash.sh as floor: false (line 163).
findings.description: The floor is documented as 'the set of guards ... no profile, knob or cycle task may weaken', enforced by floor-snapshot.bats comparing floor_files byte-for-byte to origin/main. But the script that implements every fence floor guard (block-destructive-bash.sh) and the settings.json registration that arms it are not floor files. A cycle task can add a new allow branch (e.g. widen the _c2_authorized marker check, add an env-var bypass, or drop the hook registration) without touching any floor file; the floor_corpus rows only detect changes to the expected verdict of the existing corpus commands and will not catch a new bypass condition that the corpus never exercises. The floor therefore protects guard identifiers, not the guard behaviour, and the register would still report floor: true for guards whose enforcement was removed.
findings.failure_mode: A cycle task or autonomous run edits block-destructive-bash.sh (or removes its PreToolUse:Bash registration) to weaken the State-Zone/System-Zone write fences; floor-snapshot.bats and guard-origins.bats both pass because no floor_files or floor_guards entry changed, so the weakening ships with the floor still reported intact.
findings.suggested_fix: Add .claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh and .claude/settings.json (or at minimum its hooks block, via a dedicated snapshot test) to floor_files, and set floor: true on hook:safety/block-destructive-bash.sh in guard-origins.yaml. Alternatively, make floor-snapshot.bats derive the protected file set from the `script` fields of every floor: true row plus the hook file behind each floor fence, so the register and the snapshot cannot drift.

findings.description: The hook now stamps every block/bypass/allow-override audit row with replay: true whenever the LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY environment variable equals '1', across four separate jq writers (emit_block, FR-MERGE-2 override, FR-SZ bypass, FR-SZ2 marker allow). The flag is taken on trust from the process environment; nothing verifies that the hook is actually being driven by the corpus runner. Any downstream consumer that excludes replay rows (the guard-yield 30-day totals surfaced in loa-status) will silently discount real blocks whenever that variable leaks into the Claude Code session environment, for example via a settings env block, a shell profile, or a leftover export from a corpus run in the same shell.
findings.failure_mode: Real blocked destructive commands are tagged replay: true and excluded from the yield that operators and the register use to judge whether a guard is earning its keep, hiding genuine hits and possibly leading to a guard being demoted or removed.
findings.suggested_fix: Tie the replay flag to something the corpus runner alone controls, e.g. a nonce file path or token passed in the hook stdin payload by run-corpus.sh, or have run-corpus.sh write to a separate audit file (LOA_AUDIT_FILE) instead of tagging rows in the live .run/audit.jsonl. At minimum, have guard-yield.sh report the replay-row count alongside the totals so a leak is visible.

findings.description: The implementing-tasks skill's app zone permission is widened from read to read-write in the same change that introduces the floor register. This is consistent with the documented intent that /implement is the sanctioned writer of app code, so it is probably a correction rather than a regression, but it is an unexplained permission expansion with no accompanying note, test or guard-origins entry, and nothing in the visible diff shows what consumes the zones: frontmatter (if it is prose-only, the change widens what the model believes it may do without any harness change).
findings.failure_mode: If any tooling (validate-skill-capabilities.sh, zone guards, review checks) keys off zones.app.permission, app writes under /implement now pass where they previously would have been asked about; if nothing consumes it, the widening is undocumented drift that later audits cannot distinguish from an accidental grant.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the reason for the change in the PR or a DEC row, confirm which scripts read zones.*.permission, and add a bats assertion that only implementing-tasks (and the bug workflow) carry app: read-write so future widenings in other skills are caught.

findings.description: Two pieces of explicit security guidance are removed from the reviewer prompt: the zone constraint no longer states that .claude/ is never edited and grimoires/.beads are state, and the checklist no longer enumerates red flags (private keys, SQL concatenation, unvalidated input, empty catch blocks) inline, deferring both to REFERENCE.md and CLAUDE.loa.md. These are prose-class guards, so the harness fences still apply, but the review skill now depends on the model actually opening REFERENCE.md for the red-flag list, which it is not instructed to do unconditionally.
findings.failure_mode: A review pass under context pressure skips REFERENCE.md and no longer has the red-flag checklist in its working prompt, lowering recall for the exact categories (secrets, injection, input validation) the security review is meant to catch.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep a one-line pointer that makes reading REFERENCE.md §Security a required step (e.g. in the Phase 2 steps), or keep the short red-flag enumeration inline since it costs few bytes relative to the prompt budget.

findings.description: stash-safety.md gains a paths: frontmatter scoping it to shell, bats, scripts and hooks files. If the rules loader honours paths (the new tests/unit/rule-paths.bats suggests it does), the rule is no longer loaded when the model is working on other file types, yet the hazard it describes (git stash push/pop with swallowed output around pre-commit hooks) arises from Bash commands the model runs regardless of which files it is editing. Only the swallowed-output shape is mechanically fenced by FR-1.2b; the broader guidance (do not wrap work in stash at all inside skills) becomes conditional.
findings.failure_mode: The model runs a plain 'git stash push && ... && git stash pop' while editing, say, Python or Markdown, without the rule in context; FR-1.2b does not fire because no output is swallowed, and an overlapping pre-commit stash shifts indexes causing silent data loss.
findings.suggested_fix: Either drop paths: for this rule so it stays global, or add a glob that covers all source files, keeping the narrow scoping only for rules that genuinely concern a file type.
